skills.name: Volcanicity: benefits, hazards and human responses

note.text: Volcanic areas can provide fertile weathered soils, rock materials, landscapes that attract visitors and geothermal opportunities under suitable conditions. They can also face lava, ash, gases and fast-moving hazards. A long-term resource benefit does not make an eruption safe. Risk depends on the hazard and people's exposure and vulnerability. Monitoring and official evacuation planning reduce some risks but do not guarantee precise predictions or eliminate danger.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Volcanic areas can provide fertile weathered soils, rock materials, landscapes that attract visitors and geothermal opportunities under suitable conditions. They can also face lava, ash, gases and fast-moving hazards. A long-term resource benefit does not make an eruption safe. Risk depends on the hazard and people's exposure and vulnerability. Monitoring and official evacuation planning reduce some risks but do not guarantee precise predictions or eliminate danger.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Communities near Mount Cameroon may benefit from landscapes and soils while still needing to respect hazard information. Weathering can improve some soils over time; fresh lava is not instant farmland. Tourism income also depends on access, services and safety. Avoid presenting attractive scenery as a reason to disregard local warnings.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate the natural process, a possible resource and the conditions required to use it. Compare short-term damage with long-term benefits without cancelling one out against the other. For real events follow local authorities and trained responders rather than treating a school exercise as an operational forecast.
